::: {.callout-important}
## Computer required during the course

Every student must bring a Windows, macOS or Linux laptop to every session with the tools on this page installed and working. A browser or tablet alone does not replace the local applications used in the course.

A stable Internet connection is required. 8 GB of memory is strongly recommended; 16 GB provides more comfort. If an organization manages the computer, confirm before class that you are allowed to install software.
:::

## What must work {#expected-result}

Before the first session, you must be able to confirm all seven items:

- R starts inside RStudio and runs `1 + 1`.
- RStudio Desktop opens a project and a `.qmd` file.
- Quarto responds to `quarto check`.
- Git responds to `git --version`.
- your GitHub account exists and its email address is verified;
- `ssh -T git@github.com` recognizes your account;
- a Quarto document containing R code produces an HTML file without an error.

::: {.callout-note}
## Where to enter commands

R commands go in RStudio's Console tab. The `git`, `quarto`, `ssh` and `ls` commands go in a terminal. On Windows, use Git Bash after installing Git. On macOS or Linux, use Terminal. RStudio's Terminal pane also works when available.
:::

## Installation order {#installation-order}

Follow this order. RStudio uses R, Quarto runs R code and Git also provides Git Bash on Windows.

### 1. Install R

Download R from the [Comprehensive R Archive Network](https://cran.r-project.org/), then choose your system:

- [R for Windows](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)
- [R for macOS](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/)
- [R for Linux](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/)

Accept the default installation options. On macOS, choose the file that matches the computer's processor when several installers are offered.

You will verify R inside RStudio after the next step.

### 2. Install RStudio Desktop

Download the free version of [RStudio Desktop from Posit](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). Close and reopen RStudio after installation.

In the Console tab, run:

```r
R.version.string
1 + 1
```

The first result must display an R version and the second must display `2`.

### 3. Install Quarto

Download the installer for your system from the [official Quarto download page](https://quarto.org/docs/download/). Close RStudio completely, reopen it, then run in the terminal:

```bash
quarto --version
quarto check
```

The first command must display a version number. The second must detect Quarto and an R installation without a blocking error.

### 4. Install Git {.tabset}

#### Windows

Download [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win), run the installer and keep the default choices. Open Git Bash, then run:

```bash
git --version
```

#### macOS

Open Terminal and run:

```bash
git --version
```

If macOS offers to install the command-line tools, accept and let installation finish. You can also use the [Git installer for macOS](https://git-scm.com/download/mac). Run `git --version` again after installation.

#### Linux

Use your distribution's package manager. For Debian or Ubuntu:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install git
git --version
```

For Fedora:

```bash
sudo dnf install git
git --version
```

The official documentation lists [other Linux options](https://git-scm.com/download/linux).

## Configure Git and GitHub {#configure-git-github}

### 5. Create and verify the GitHub account

Create a free personal account with the [official GitHub procedure](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/start-your-journey/creating-an-account-on-github). Use an email address you check and complete the verification sent by GitHub.

Write down your exact GitHub username. You will use it in several course activities.

### 6. Record your Git identity

In the terminal, replace both values with your name and the address linked to your GitHub account:

```bash
git config --global user.name "First Last"
git config --global user.email "address-linked-to-github@example.com"
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global --list
```

Check that `user.name`, `user.email` and `init.defaultbranch=main` contain the correct values. This information will be associated with your commits.

### 7. Configure SSH access to GitHub

SSH lets Git communicate with GitHub without asking for your password for every operation. The complete official procedure is in [Connecting to GitHub with SSH](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh).

First check whether a key already exists:

```bash
ls -al ~/.ssh
```

If a file such as `id_ed25519.pub` already exists and is linked to your GitHub account, do not create a second key. Otherwise, create one after replacing the email address:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "address-linked-to-github@example.com"
```

Press Enter to accept the proposed location. A passphrase is recommended. Then load the key for the active session:

```bash
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

Copy only the public key:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
#### Windows, Git Bash

```bash
clip < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
#### macOS

```bash
pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```
:::

::: {.column width="34%"}
#### Linux

```bash
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```

Copy the complete displayed line.
:::
::::

In GitHub, open `Settings > SSH and GPG keys > New SSH key`, give the computer a recognizable title, paste the public key and save it. Then test:

```bash
ssh -T git@github.com
```

On the first connection, confirm the host fingerprint if GitHub asks. The expected result contains `successfully authenticated` and your username. The message stating that GitHub does not provide shell access is normal.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Never share the private key

The `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` file is private. Do not copy it to GitHub, Brio, email or a help request. Only the file ending in `.pub` may be shared.
:::

## Install the starting R packages {#r-packages}

Run this complete block in the RStudio Console. It installs only the missing packages required at the start of the course, followed by the `UlavalSSD` data package used in Module 1.

```r
# Core packages for the first activities
required_packages <- c("tidyverse", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "remotes")

installed_packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
missing_packages <- setdiff(required_packages, installed_packages)

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_packages)
}

# Course data package
if (!requireNamespace("UlavalSSD", quietly = TRUE)) {
  remotes::install_github("AurelienNicosiaULaval/UlavalSSD")
}
```

Then verify:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(UlavalSSD)

dim(UlavalSSD::MeteoQuebec)
```

The result must display two numbers, the number of rows and the number of columns. Other packages will be installed when the modules use them; the [R Packages](packages.html) page lists them.

## Final test with a Quarto document {#final-test}

In RStudio, choose `File > New File > Quarto Document`. Create an HTML document, replace its contents with the text below and save it as `installation-test.qmd`:

````{=html}
<pre><code>---
title: "STT-1100 installation test"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
---

This document confirms that R, RStudio, Quarto and the packages work together.

&#96;&#96;&#96;{r}
library(tidyverse)

results &lt;- tibble(
  value = 1:3,
  square = value^2
)

results
&#96;&#96;&#96;</code></pre>
````

Click `Render`. The installation is ready when:

1. no red error interrupts rendering;
2. an `installation-test.html` file is created and opens;
3. the `square` column contains 1, 4 and 9;
4. all four commands below give the expected results in the terminal.

```bash
git --version
quarto --version
quarto check
ssh -T git@github.com
```

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | Check | Most likely correction |
|---|---|---|
| RStudio opens, but R does not start | Run `R.version.string` in the Console | Install R before RStudio, then restart RStudio. |
| `quarto: command not found` | Run `quarto --version` in a new terminal | Install Quarto, then close and reopen the terminal and RStudio. |
| `git: command not found` | Run `git --version` | Install Git and open a new terminal. On Windows, use Git Bash. |
| `Permission denied (publickey)` | Run `ssh -T git@github.com` | Confirm that the `.pub` public key was added to the correct GitHub account and the private key is loaded. |
| `there is no package called ...` | Run `installed.packages()` in R | Install the package in the Console, then add the correct `library()` to the `.qmd` file. |
| The document works line by line, but not with `Render` | Restart R, then render again | Add every required `library()` and every object-creation step to the document. |

If the problem continues, keep:

- the operating system and its version;
- the output of `R.version.string`;
- the output of `quarto check`;
- the output of `git --version`;
- the complete error message;
- a screenshot showing the step where the problem appears.

Never send a password, access token or private SSH key.
